question: Whether WinINet's capture keeps a request its server challenges for credentials, and the request WinINet then sends with them, as one exchange or as two, and what it keeps of the credentials - with the client giving WinINet its credentials when it connects, or only once challenged.
answer: As two, each an exchange of its own: the request challenged and its 401 - a head naming Basic and an empty body - under one number, and the request WinINet then sent with the credentials, and its answer, under another, begun once the challenge's response ended, every time. No record ties the two. WinINet answered a challenge by itself where its client gave it credentials when it connected, and sent the request again once a client that gave them only when challenged set them and sent it; either way, once a challenge was answered it sent the credentials with every later request to that server unasked, so only each client's first request was challenged - one of 16, or eight of 64 eight clients at once. The capture keeps the Authorization field as WinINet sent it: Basic credentials, a user name and password encoded, not encrypted. Every part matched the server's truth, and nothing was lost.

probe.tool: tools/InterCat.WinInetProbe --auth basic|basic-late [--tls] [--async] [--concurrency 8 --requests 64 --ledger], 16 requests each or 64 eight at once, beside a decoy outside the process filter; the server answers each request without the run's test credentials - made for the fixture's own loopback server, secret to nothing - with a 401 of no body naming Basic, and logs each leg apart

runs.run: credentials given when the client connects
credentials given once challenged, the request sent again
eight at once, its buffers' metadata kept
given once challenged, eight at once, its buffers' metadata kept

capture.command: icat record --profile content --source etw/manifest/Microsoft-Windows-WinINet-Capture --mechanism http --pid <workload> --channel * --max-record-bytes 65536 --max-session-bytes 67108864 --inspection hex-text --duration 25, beside InterCat.TestWorkloads http-wininet --requests 64 --start-after 8 --auth basic|basic-late --concurrency 8; then icat exchanges --exchanges 10000 --decode, and each part of each exchange saved by icat content --part and matched by SHA-256 with the server's truth of its leg

runs.run: credentials given when the client connects, eight at once
credentials given once challenged, eight at once

ledger: fixtures/FX-HTTP-011/evidence/basic-eight-at-once/buffers.csv and basic-late-eight-at-once/buffers.csv: each buffer the probe captured of its 64 requests' 72 exchanges, in time order - its 100 ns readings after the first, event, exchange number, place, ends, length, the request its exchange's head named, whether a thread that made a request raised it, and its leg: the one the server challenged, or the one carrying credentials - never its bytes. A test groups each as a session's records are grouped, rebuilds each head from the scenario and checks it against the server's truth byte for byte, and holds each challenge to its own answer and each request carrying credentials to what it says of them.
note: A challenge's response body is empty, and kept as one buffer of no byte; request 0's empty body raises no record in either leg. WinINet's own answer to a challenge, and each request carrying credentials unasked, keep the request's fields in their order with the Authorization field last; a request its client sent again once challenged takes the client's added field anew, after WinINet's own, and the credentials after it. The credentials are test values made for the fixture's own loopback server; neither the truth nor this file holds a byte of what was sent or read.
